setupGuide.title: Set up your PagerDuty OAuth connection

steps.title: Open PagerDuty developer apps
steps.description: Go to PagerDuty Developer -> Applications and create or open the OAuth app you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Install the OAuth app on your PagerDuty account
steps.description: Make sure the app is installed on the same PagerDuty account you plan to connect from. The connection subdomain must match the part before .pagerduty.com in your PagerDuty URL.

steps.title: Copy your client credentials
steps.description: Copy the app's Client ID and Client Secret from PagerDuty.

steps.title: Enter the connection fields in MindCloud
steps.description: In MindCloud, enter the Client ID, Client Secret, your PagerDuty subdomain, and the PagerDuty user email that should be sent in the From header for incident updates.

steps.title: Authenticate the connection
steps.description: Save or reconnect the MindCloud PagerDuty connection so MindCloud can request an OAuth access token using the client credentials flow.

steps.description: Go to the official Pappers API page and start account creation.

steps.title: Create and confirm your API account
steps.description: Sign up with a professional email address and complete the email confirmation flow.

steps.title: Copy your API token

steps.title: Check your available credits

name: Papyrs
description: Papyrs is a company intranet and document management platform. This wrapper lets agents list pages, read page content, manage page widgets, search content, access people records, and post to activity feeds from a Papyrs workspace.

authentication.name: API Token
authentication.description: Connect Papyrs with a generated API token and your Papyrs subdomain.
authentication.notes: Papyrs requires both a generated API token and the workspace subdomain. Requests authenticate with the `auth_token` query parameter, and the official docs state a default rate limit of 6 requests per 60 seconds.

credentials.name: Subdomain

setupGuide.title: Connect Papyrs with an API token

steps.title: Request API access for your Papyrs account

steps.title: Generate an API token
steps.description: After API access is enabled, go to Site Settings > Integrations & SSO and click Generate Token to create a new token for the user you want to connect.

steps.title: Copy your Papyrs subdomain
steps.description: Find the subdomain from your Papyrs workspace URL. For example, if your workspace is https://company.papyrs.com, enter company as the Subdomain value in MindCloud.

setupGuide.title: Connect Payhip

steps.description: Sign in to Payhip, open Developer Settings, and copy the account API key shown there.

steps.title: Optional: copy your product secret key

authentication.notes: Create an API key in PDF Snake, then paste it here. PDF Snake accepts the key as an Authorization bearer token or as a multipart apiKey field. This app uses the bearer-token contract because it matches the provider OpenAPI and MindCloud native apiKey runtime.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud

steps.title: Verify the balance endpoint

arguments.description: Custom referral parameter appended as '?ref=' for downstream attribution and analysis.

steps.description: Confirm you can sign in with the Pinghome account you want to connect.

steps.title: Request a bearer token from the Account Sign In endpoint
steps.description: Follow Pinghome's Account Sign In documentation and send a POST request to https://auth.api.pinghome.io/v1/auth with your email and password in the JSON body.

steps.title: Copy the access token
steps.description: From the successful sign-in response, copy the access_token value. This is the bearer token MindCloud should store.

steps.title: Paste the token into the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Use the copied access token as the Pinghome connection credential in MindCloud.

name: Pipeliner Cloud
description: Pipeliner Cloud is a CRM platform for managing accounts, contacts, opportunities, leads, activities, products, and related sales data through the Pipeliner Cloud REST API.

authentication.name: Basic Authentication
authentication.description: Use the Pipeliner API application username and password with the service URL and space ID from Show API Access.

credentials.name: Service URL
credentials.description: The regional Pipeliner service URL shown in API Access, for example https://us-east.api.pipelinersales.com.

credentials.name: Space ID
credentials.description: The Pipeliner space ID shown in API Access. This is appended to every REST API request path.

setupGuide.title: Set up Pipeliner Cloud credentials
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need admin access to the Pipeliner space you want to connect.

steps.title: Sign in to Pipeliner CRM
steps.description: Open the Pipeliner CRM sign-in page and log in to the space you want to connect in MindCloud.

steps.title: Open the Applications administration page
steps.description: From the space administration area, open the Unit, Users & Roles section and then open Applications.

steps.title: Create or open an API application
steps.description: Create a new Application if one does not already exist for this connection.

steps.title: Open Show API Access
steps.description: Select Show API Access for the application and copy the User Name, Password, Service URL, and Space ID values.

steps.title: Enter the values in MindCloud
steps.description: When creating the MindCloud connection, paste the API application username, password, service URL, and space ID exactly as shown by Pipeliner.

setupGuide.title: Connect and Use Plaid
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Start with Plaid Sandbox credentials. Live use also requires the right product access in Plaid Dashboard, and OAuth institutions require an allowlisted HTTPS redirect URI before you switch to Production credentials.

steps.title: Find your Plaid keys
steps.description: Sign in to Plaid Dashboard, open Team Settings > Keys, and copy the Client ID plus the Secret for the environment you want to use.

steps.title: Connect with Sandbox credentials first
steps.description: Paste the Sandbox Client ID and Sandbox Secret into this connection first. This Plaid app is configured against the Sandbox API during build and test work.

steps.title: Enable the Plaid products you plan to use
steps.description: In Plaid Dashboard, request or enable the products your workflows need. This app has been built around Transactions, Auth, Identity, Liabilities, Investments, Recurring Transactions, Transactions Refresh, and Enrich.

steps.title: Fastest Sandbox path to an access token
steps.description: Run Create Sandbox Public Token, then run Exchange Public Token with the returned public token. The exchange response gives you the item access token used by most account, transaction, identity, liability, and investment actions.

steps.title: Link or browser path to an access token
steps.description: If you are testing the real Link flow, run Create Link Token, complete Plaid Link in your client, collect the returned public token, and then run Exchange Public Token.

steps.title: Use the returned access token in product actions
steps.description: Reuse the access token returned by Exchange Public Token when you run actions such as Get Accounts, Get Transactions, Get Identity, Get Liabilities, or investment actions.

steps.title: Prepare live OAuth institutions only if you need them
steps.description: If you plan to use live OAuth institutions, allowlist your redirect URI in Plaid Dashboard and complete Plaid's registration steps before switching to Production credentials.

name: PostgreSQL
description: Store data, run queries, build applications, and handle complex workloads.

setupGuide.title: Set up your PostgreSQL connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need the PostgreSQL host, database name, user name, and password for the account MindCloud should use. If your server requires TLS verification, also get the CA/root certificate and any SSL instructions from your database administrator or hosting provider.

steps.title: Collect the PostgreSQL connection details
steps.description: Get the Host, Database, User, and Password values for the PostgreSQL database you want MindCloud to access. If your administrator uses a non-default server port, get that Port value as well.

steps.title: Enter the basic connection fields in MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud PostgreSQL connection form, enter Host, Port, Database, User, and Password exactly as provided. If your administrator did not give you a custom port, you can leave Port empty and use the server default.

steps.title: Configure SSL only if your PostgreSQL server requires it
steps.description: Turn on SSL when your server requires an encrypted connection. If your administrator provided a trusted CA/root certificate for server verification, paste it into Certificate and keep Reject Unauthorized enabled so the server certificate is validated against that trusted certificate.

steps.title: Fill in advanced options only when your environment calls for them
steps.description: Set Timeout only if you need to limit how long the connection waits before failing. Leave Use ODBC off unless your PostgreSQL environment specifically requires the official psqlODBC driver.

steps.title: Open Personal API keys in your PostHog account settings

steps.title: Create a new personal API key

steps.title: Copy the new key immediately
steps.description: Copy the personal API key value as soon as it appears. PostHog does not show the full key again after you leave or refresh the page.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud

your template Project into the newly created Project.

ProjectManager-supplied templates.

actions.name: Create Task
actions.description: Creates a new task in ProjectManager.

arguments.name: Project Id
arguments.description: The unique identifier of the Project that will contain this Task

arguments.name: Name
arguments.description: The common name of this Task.

arguments.name: Description
arguments.description: A description of the work to be performed in this Task.

arguments.name: Percent Complete
arguments.description:
The numerical percentage, from 0-100, representing the percentage completion
for this Task.  Any numbers below zero or above 100 will be clamped to the
minimum or maximum value.
            
This value can be edited manually in the Gantt chart view of the application,
or can be selected on the Task Detail page within the Kanban board.

arguments.name: Status Id
arguments.description: The unique identifier of the TaskStatus for this Task

arguments.name: Priority Id
arguments.description: A numerical value representing the Priority of this Task

arguments.name: Assignees
arguments.description: A list of unique identifiers of TaskAssignees to be assigned to this Task

arguments.description: The date when work on this Task is planned to begin.

arguments.name: Planned Finish Date
arguments.description: The date when work on this Task is expected to complete.

arguments.name: Planned Duration
arguments.description: The planned duration (in minutes) for this Task.  Cannot be negative.

arguments.name: Planned Effort
arguments.description: The planned effort (in minutes) for this Task.  Cannot be negative.

arguments.name: Planned Cost
arguments.description: The planned cost for this Task.  Cannot be negative.

arguments.name: Actual Start Date
arguments.description: The date when work on this Task actually started, if known.

arguments.name: Actual Cost
arguments.description: The actual cost of this Task to date, if known.

arguments.name: Theme
arguments.description:
Color theme definition for this task.
            
eg. Blue, Brown, DarkBlue, DarkGrey, Gold, Green, Grey, LightBrown, LightGreen,
LightGrey, LightPurple, LightYellow, Magenta, Mauve, Navy, Orange, Purple, Red.

arguments.name: Is Locked
arguments.description:
Unlocked tasks can be adjusted by changes to their dependencies, resource leveling, or other factors.
            
All tasks are unlocked by default.
            
If a task is set to `IsLocked` = `true`, the dates and assigned resources are locked for this task and will not
be automatically changed by any process.

arguments.name: Is Milestone
arguments.description:
True if this task is a milestone.  Milestones represent a specific point in time for the project.  When a
milestone is locked, it represents a fixed time within the project that can be used to relate to other tasks.

arguments.name: Parent Id
arguments.description:
Gets or sets the unique identifier of the parent task.
If set, this task will be a child of the specified parent task, supporting task hierarchies and sub-tasks.

arguments.name: Index
arguments.description:
Gets or sets the position of the task within the list of project tasks.
Used to determine the order of tasks in the project with the first task being 1.

arguments.description: The unique identifier of the Task to update

arguments.name: Name
arguments.description: The common name of this Task.

arguments.name: Description
arguments.description: A description of the work to be performed in this Task.

arguments.name: Percent Complete
arguments.description:
The numerical percentage, from 0-100, representing the percentage completion
for this Task.  Any numbers below zero or above 100 will be clamped to the
minimum or maximum value.
            
This value can be edited manually in the Gantt chart view of the application,
or can be selected on the Task Detail page within the Kanban board.

arguments.name: Status Id
arguments.description: The TaskStatus assigned to this Task.

arguments.name: Priority Id
arguments.description: The unique identifier of the TaskPriority

arguments.name: Planned Start Date
arguments.description:
The date when work on this Task is planned to begin.
            
This value contains only the date in year-month-day format.  For display, this
date will always be shown as this same year-month-day regardless of time zone.
For reporting purposes, this date is calculated against the official time zone
of the Workspace.
            
For example: A Task has a planned completion date of July 5, 2023 in a Workspace
that has a time zone of US Pacific Time (GMT-7 or GMT-8, depending on daylight
savings time).  This project is considered overdue on 12:01 AM July 6th 2023 in
US Pacific time.

arguments.name: Planned Finish Date
arguments.description:

date will always be shown as this same year-month-day regardless of time zone.

of the Workspace.

that has a time zone of US Pacific Time (GMT-7 or GMT-8, depending on daylight
savings time).  This project is considered overdue on 12:01 AM July 6th 2023 in
US Pacific time.

arguments.description: The planned duration (in minutes) for this Task.  Cannot be negative.

name: ProvenExpert
description: Collect reviews, send invites, and share rating widgets

authentication.name: Basic
authentication.description: Authenticate with your ProvenExpert API ID and API key.

setupGuide.title: Connect ProvenExpert
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a ProvenExpert account with API access enabled for the profile you want to connect.

steps.title: Open Developer API in ProvenExpert
steps.description: Sign in to ProvenExpert, open Administration, and then open Developer API for the profile you want to connect.

steps.title: Copy the API ID and API key
steps.description: Copy the API ID and API key shown on the Developer API page. ProvenExpert uses the API ID as the username and the API key as the password for Basic authentication.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: In MindCloud, paste the API ID into the Username field and the API key into the Password field, then run Test Connection.
